title: [Decision] @secuura/shared is imported by 24 services and declared by 2 — the symlink pattern is invisible to every lockfile and audit gate
description:
## BLUF

**24 services import** `@secuura/shared`**. Only 2 declare it. The other 22 resolve it because a Dockerfile creates a symlink — which means the dependency is invisible to** `npm ls`**, to** `npm audit`**, to the lockfile gates, and to anyone reading a** `package.json` **to learn what a service depends on.**

Spun out of [KS-647](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-647) so that ticket can close on its actual scope (flipping mcp-server + vc-issuer to `npm ci`, which needs none of this). **This ticket is the design decision underneath it.**

## The measurement — `develop 2129cdc8b`, 2026-08-17

|  | Count | Detail |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Services importing `@secuura/shared` in source | **25** | incl. `services/shared` itself |
| Service Dockerfiles creating `ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared` | **24** | the resolution mechanism |
| Services **declaring** it in `package.json` | **2** | `mcp-server`, `vc-issuer` — both as `"*"` |
| Services importing it with **no declaration** | **22** | analytics, anchoring, api-gateway, auth, billing, demo-service, governance, guardian, kyc, m365-integration, nft-certificate, originate, prism, queue, referral, security, staking, tenant-provisioning, timestamping, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector |

The root `package.json` declares `workspaces: ["packages/*","services/*","frontend/*"]`, so this resolves cleanly at dev time via the workspace hoist. **The Docker build does not use the workspace root** — each service builds from its own context with its own `package.json` and standalone lockfile — so the symlink is what makes it work in an image.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

It works today, and the pattern is deliberate and consistent. The cost is in what it hides:

1. **Audit blindness.** `@secuura/shared` and anything it depends on appear in no service lockfile. The KS-470 audit gate and the KS-531 standalone-lock audit both read manifests and lockfiles — neither can see this edge. A vulnerability reachable only through `@secuura/shared` would be invisible to both gates.
2. **No version pinning.** Nothing records which version of the shared package a service was built against. `packages/shared` is at `0.3.0`; no consumer references that, so a breaking change in the shared package is discoverable only by rebuilding and booting each service.
3. **It is not self-describing.** Reading `services/auth/package.json` does not tell you the service depends on `@secuura/shared`. Twenty-two services are in that position.
4. **The two exceptions prove it is confusing.** `mcp-server` and `vc-issuer` declared the dependency — the intuitively correct thing — and that is precisely why they cannot use `npm ci`, and why they carry `sed -i` lines to undo their own manifests.

## Options (not a recommendation — this is the decision to take)

**A. Formalise the workspace.** Declare `"@secuura/shared": "workspace:*"` and build service images from the workspace root rather than per-service contexts. Correct and self-describing; the cost is a change to every service Dockerfile's build context and probably the CI image-build matrix.

**B. Publish** `packages/shared` **to a private registry** (GitHub Packages on the existing org). Every service declares a real version, locks resolve normally, audit tooling sees the tree. The cost is a publish step in CI and a registry credential in every build.

**C. Keep the symlink, make it visible.** Leave the mechanism alone but add `@secuura/shared` to a documented allowlist that the audit tooling explicitly accounts for, so the blind spot is recorded rather than accidental. Cheapest; does not fix pinning.

**D. Do nothing, deliberately.** Defensible while the shared package is small and changes with its consumers. Should then be written down as a decision, because right now it reads as an accident.

## Acceptance

A decision recorded with its reasoning, and — whichever option — the audit blind spot either closed or explicitly documented in `scripts/audit/`, so a future reader does not assume the lockfile gates cover this edge when they do not.

## Not urgent

No known vulnerability rides on this today. Filed so the design question stops being rediscovered every time someone touches a Dockerfile — it has now surfaced through KS-374, KS-384 and KS-647.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row B6 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option C now, with A as the target: keep the current link to the shared code library but document it and teach the audit about it, which is the cheapest way to close the audit blind spot; later formalise the workspace (A).

The ticket's counts (22 services use the shared library without listing it) come from 2026-08-17; today's count is not measured. A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.
